title: Introduction
text: R package starsExtra provides several miscellaneous functions working stars objects, mainly single-band rasters. Currently includes functions : Focal filtering Detrending Digital Elevation Models Calculating flow length Calculating Convergence Index Calculating topographic slope Calculating topographic aspect

text: following code applied 15*15 mean focal filter 533*627 stars Digital Elevation Model (DEM): calculation takes: 0.5625446 secs. original DEM filtered DEM can combined plotted following expressions:
code: data(carmel) carmel_mean15 = focal2(   x = carmel,             # Input 'stars' raster   w = matrix(1, 15, 15),  # Weights   fun = "mean",           # Aggregation function   na.rm = TRUE,           # 'NA' in neighborhood are removed   mask = TRUE             # Areas that were 'NA' in 'x' are masked from result ) r = c(carmel, carmel_mean15, along = 3) r = st_set_dimensions(r, 3, values = c("input", "15*15 mean filter")) plot(r, breaks = "equal", col = terrain.colors(10), key.pos = 4)

title: Miscellaneous Functions for Working with stars Rasters
text: following code section compares calculation time focal2 example raster::focal (using C/C++) reference method focal2r (using R code ).
code: library(microbenchmark) library(starsExtra) library(raster)  data(carmel) carmelr = as(carmel, "Raster")  res = microbenchmark(   focal2 = focal2(carmel, w = matrix(1, 15, 15), fun = "mean", na.rm = FALSE),    focal = focal(carmelr, w = matrix(1, 15, 15), fun = mean, na.rm = FALSE),   focal2r = focal2r(carmel, w = matrix(1, 15, 15), mean),   times = 10 ) res #> Unit: milliseconds #>     expr        min         lq       mean     median         uq        max neval #>   focal2   542.3506   546.0164   587.9224   554.3557   609.8761   793.5663    10 #>    focal   114.3561   115.9764   142.2213   119.7932   125.9327   339.7064    10 #>  focal2r 17236.5407 17367.5100 17734.2765 17634.1378 17902.5663 19048.0060    10 boxplot(res)

title: Calculate the Convergence Index (CI) from a slope raster — CI
Calculate the Convergence Index (CI) from a slope raster — CI
text: x raster (class stars) two dimensions: x y, .e., single-band raster, representing aspect decimal degrees clockwise north, possibly including -1 specify flat terrain, returned function aspect. k k Neighborhood size around focal cell. Must odd number. example, k=3 implies 3*3 neighborhood. na.rm NA values ignored calculating CI? Default FALSE, .e., least one aspect value neighborhood NA CI also set NA. na_flag Value used mark NA values C code. set value guaranteed absent input raster x (default -9999).

title: Calculate the Convergence Index (CI) from a slope raster — CI
text: stars raster CI values.

title: Calculate the Convergence Index (CI) from a slope raster — CI
text: raster "padded" (k-1)/2 rows columns NA values sides, neighborhood outermost rows columns still complete neighborhood. rows columns removed final result returning . Aspect values -1, specifying flat terrain, assigned CI value 0 regardless neighboring values.

title: Calculate the Convergence Index (CI) from a slope raster — CI
text: Convergence Index algorithm described : Thommeret, N., Bailly, J. S., & Puech, C. (2010). Extraction thalweg networks DTMs: application badlands.

title: Calculate the Convergence Index (CI) from a slope raster — CI
code: # Small example data(dem) dem_asp = aspect(dem) dem_ci = CI(dem_asp, k = 3) r = c(dem, round(dem_ci, 1), along = 3) r = st_set_dimensions(r, 3, values = c("input (aspect)", "output (CI, k=3)")) plot(r, text_values = TRUE, breaks = "equal", col = terrain.colors(10), mfrow = c(1, 2))  # \donttest{ # Larger example data(golan) golan_asp = aspect(golan) golan_ci = CI(golan_asp, k = 25) plot(golan_asp, breaks = "equal", col = hcl.colors(11, "Spectral"), main = "input (aspect)")  plot(golan_ci, breaks = "equal", col = hcl.colors(11, "Spectral"), main = "output (CI, k=25)")  # }

text: Calculates flow length pixel Digital Elevation Model (DEM) raster. Inputs output rasters class stars, single-band (.e., `"x"` `"y"` dimensions), one attribute.

title: Calculate flow length — flowlength
Calculate flow length — flowlength
text: elev numeric stars raster representing Digital Elevation Model (DEM). veg matching logical stars raster representing vegetation presence. TRUE values represent vegetated cells flow absorbed (.e. sinks), FALSE values represent cells flow unobstructed. progress Display progress bar? default TRUE

title: Calculate flow length — flowlength
text: numeric stars raster cell value flow length, resolution units.

title: Calculate flow length — flowlength
text: algorithm described : Mayor, . G., Bautista, S., Small, E. E., Dixon, M., & Bellot, J. (2008). Measurement connectivity runoff source areas determined vegetation pattern topography: tool assessing potential water soil losses drylands. Water Resources Research, 44(10).

title: Calculate flow length — flowlength
code: # Example from Fig. 2 in Mayor et al. 2008  elev = rbind(   c(8, 8, 8, 8, 9, 8, 9),   c(7, 7, 7, 7, 9, 7, 7),   c(6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 5, 7),   c(4, 5, 5, 3, 5, 4, 7),   c(4, 5, 4, 5, 4, 6, 5),   c(3, 3, 3, 3, 2, 3, 3),   c(2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 1, 3) ) veg = rbind(   c(TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  FALSE, FALSE, TRUE),   c(TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  FALSE, FALSE),   c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE),   c(FALSE, TRUE,  FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE),   c(TRUE,  TRUE,  FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE),   c(TRUE,  TRUE,  TRUE,  FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE),   c(FALSE, TRUE,  TRUE,  FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,  TRUE) ) elev = matrix_to_stars(elev) veg = matrix_to_stars(veg)  # Calculate flow length fl = flowlength(elev, veg, progress = FALSE)  # Plot plot(   round(elev, 1), text_values = TRUE, breaks = "equal",    col = terrain.colors(6), main = "input (elevation)" )  plot(   veg*1, text_values = TRUE, breaks = "equal",    col = rev(terrain.colors(2)), main = "input (vegetation)" )  plot(   round(fl, 1), text_values = TRUE, breaks = "equal",    col = terrain.colors(6), main = "output (flowlength)" )  # \donttest{ # Larger example data(carmel) elev = carmel elev[is.na(elev)] = 0 veg = elev > 100 fl = flowlength(elev, veg, progress = FALSE) plot(fl, breaks = "equal", col = hcl.colors(11), main = "flowlength (m)")  # }

what: Apply a focal filter on a raster — focal2
title: Apply a focal filter on a raster — focal2
text: Applies focal filter weighted neighborhood w raster. weights (w) can added , subtracted , multiplied divided raster values (specified weight_fun). focal cell taken mean, sum, minimum maximum weighted values (specified fun).  Input output rasters class stars, single-band (.e., `"x"` `"y"` dimensions), one attribute.

title: Apply a focal filter on a raster — focal2
code: focal2(   x,   w,   fun = "mean",   weight_fun = "*",   na.rm = FALSE,   mask = FALSE,   na_flag = -9999 )

title: Apply a focal filter on a raster — focal2
text: x raster (class stars) one attribute two dimensions: x y, .e., single-band raster. w Weights matrix defining neighborhood size around focal cell, well weights. example, matrix(1,3,3) implies neighborhood size 3*3 equal weights 1 cells. matrix must square, .e., odd number rows columns. fun function aggregate resulting values neighborhood. Possible values : "mean", "sum", "min", "max", "mode". default "mean", .e., resulting values per neighborhood averaged assigned new focal cell value. weight_fun operator applied pair values comprising cell value respective weight value, raster_value-weight. Possible values : "+", "-", "*", "/". default "*", .e., cell value multiplied respective weight. na.rm NA values neighborhood removed calculation? Default FALSE. mask TRUE, pixels NA input set NA output well, .e., output "masked" using input (default FALSE). na_flag Value used mark NA values C code. set value guaranteed absent input raster x (default -9999).

title: Apply a focal filter on a raster — focal2
text: filtered stars raster.

title: Apply a focal filter on a raster — focal2
text: raster "padded" (nrow(w)-1)/2 rows columns NA values sides, neighborhood outermost rows columns still complete neighborhood. rows columns removed final result returning . means, instance, outermost rows columns result NA using na.rm=FALSE.

title: Apply a focal filter on a raster — focal2
text: function interface inspired function raster::focal. C code function modified expanded version C function named applyKernel included R package spatialfil.
